findings.title: Persistent actual-allocator prefix regression and next-day canary are now present and pass
findings.evidence: The deterministic four-asset, 30-index synthetic fixture calls candidate.module_a_target with lookback=4, cap=0.30 and min_assets=4. The inspected unmodified implementation calls trailing_vol for each asset and capped_weights for the four positive-volatility assets; the tests do not substitute or monkeypatch these functions. Only opens and closes at indices 13 through 29 are replaced, strictly after cutoff 12. Both schedules include a cutoff-12 decision. The weekly fixture uses (day+1)%7 and the daily synthetic fixture sets every weekday to 6.
findings.prefix_assertions: Both causal cases compare NAV entries for days 5 through 12 inclusive, all decisions through day 12 including a required cutoff decision, and all trace rows through day 12, covering modeled cash, fills and holdings. simulate appends its first NAV at lo+1=5, so [:cutoff-start] includes cutoff 12.
findings.canary_assertions: Both deliberately next-day allocator cases require identical earlier decisions but different cutoff-12 weights after future prices change. NAV remains identical through cutoff 12 because the cutoff decision executes on the next opening. The passing cases demonstrate that the persistent decision assertion detects this deliberate leak even when NAV-prefix comparison alone does not.
findings.limits: One deterministic synthetic path under two schedules, not exhaustive allocator or numerical-domain proof. The daily fixture is synthetic scheduling coverage, not a production calendar change.
